newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania parliament backs government economic plan.
newsitem.headline: Romania parliament backs government economic plan.

text.p: Romania's parliament on Wednesday approved the new reformist government and its economic plan intended to pull the country out of crisis and move towards membership of NATO and the European Union.

Members at a session voted 316 to 152 to confirm Bucharest Mayor Victor Ciorbea as Romania's youngest prime minister at the head of a 27-strong team after centrists ousted ex-communists in last month's general election.

"The election and your vote today show the Romanian people's political maturity," Ciorbea said after a five-hour debate. "It is not lessons on democracy we need, but responsible leaders, plenty of work, a competent parliament and a bit of luck."

The 120-page programme contained few specific targets for inflation, the budget deficit and most other key indicators, but called for faster privatisation and restructuring of industry, tax cuts and increased social benefits.
Ciorbea described the document as a "political programme" and said he wanted annual growth of 4.5 to six percent. He and his ministers are to be sworn in on Thursday by President Emil Constantinescu.
Leaders of the ousted leftist government, which backed cautious reforms, opposed the plan, saying it contained little concrete.
